title: Why Yawning Is Contagious
desc: A stranger yawns across a late train, and a moment later your own jaw begins to stretch. Why? In this calm, sourced long listen we travel home with one imagined man, Oskar, and look at what researchers have found about yawning. We cover how long a yawn lasts and what the body does around it, the oxygen theory put to the test in 1987, week-long yawn diaries, boredom and the colour bar experiment, yawning before birth, the brain cooling hypothesis from forehead packs to Vienna and Florida streets, yawn length and brain size across 101 species, contagion from videos, reading and thinking, why people differ, a Nottingham study of the urge to yawn, children and attention, closeness and the unsettled empathy question, virtual reality and being watched, chimpanzees, bonobos, lions and dogs. We finish with a few gentle takeaways and a slow wind-down. This video is for learning and is not medical advice; if you yawn far more than usual or feel very sleepy in the daytime, please talk to a doctor.
